title: upgrade-attn-flashattnv2-rope-fused-kv-batching-scheduling
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: Replace legacy attention kernels with a tuned FlashAttentionV2 variant and introduce fused rotary/rope ops, KV-friendly fused projections, and scheduler hooks for continuous batching to reduce p99 latency and token cost under typical Redwood workloads. Summary of changes: upgraded CUDA kernels (flashattn_v2) with fused rotary/rope support, added fused qkv projection path that writes KV cache in a single kernel, introduced optional inter-op fused ops for rotary/rope to reduce memory traffic, extended KV cache layout and eviction APIs to support continuous batching and cross-request KV reuse, and added scheduler instrumentation to support priority-based micro-batching and non-blocking KV flushes. Benchmarks: on our internal Llama-2-13B-like profile we see ~22% p50 improvement and ~18% p99 improvement on A100 for 2048 context with typical prompt distributions and a ~12% token cost reduction due to better batching and KV reuse. Backwards compatibility: maintains existing model config flags; new kernels are gated behind feature flags and runtime capability checks; fallback to previous kernels when device capability or model config is incompatible. Testing and validation: extended unit tests for fused ops and KV layout, added e2e perf bench in tests/bench/attn_perf.py, CI GPU suite run included. Rollout plan: staged canary on Dedicated pool -> 10% traffic on hosted -> full rollout, with an automatic fallback policy in serving/router for any regression >5% p99. Checklist: ensure kernel fallbacks, add config knobs, update model catalog entries, notify infra for driver minimums. Related: ENG-2148 upgrade attention kernels, ENG-2201 continuous batching scheduler hooks.
commits: feat(attn): add FlashAttentionV2 CUDA kernel implementation with fused rotary support
perf(attn): fused qkv projection kernel that writes keys/values to KV cache
feat(kv): extend KV cache layout and add eviction/timestamp hooks for continuous batching
feat(scheduler): add priority micro-batching and non-blocking KV flush paths
test: add attn perf benchmarks and unit tests for fused ops and KV layouts
ci: add gpu-integration workflow for flashattn_v2 compatibility checks
docs: runtime notes on enabling new kernels and driver requirements
fix: fallback path when device lacks fp16 atomic ops

Marisol Ortega (2026-02-16): Benchmarks look promising, but can we add a canary rollout plan and metric alerts? Please include regression guard for p99 latency.
Priya Nair (2026-02-17): Added rollout plan and automatic rollback policy when p99 increases by >5%. Added alerting guidance in docs/runtime/attn_kernels.md.
Tomás Silva (2026-02-20): Minor comments on naming and a request to document the new KV layout for platform teams. Approved pending docs and CI green.

ci_summary: CI: linux-unit, linux-integration, gpu-integration, lint. Initial gpu-integration run showed a flaky bench; rerun completed successfully. Full suite green on merge.
release_notes: Performance: Upgraded attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused rotary/rope and fused qkv->KV write path, improving p50/p99 and reducing token cost; Behavior: No breaking API changes, feature guarded by runtime flags; Ops: Requires minimum NVIDIA driver X.Y and CUDA 11.8+; Rollout: staged canary with automatic fallback on regressions.
risk_assessment: Medium: kernel changes are low-level and could cause subtle numerical differences; mitigations include per-model rollout, numeric tolerance tests, and a robust fallback path to previous kernels. Regression guard will monitor p99 and correctness metrics.
